Heat advisory for Saturday; rain continues into next week
It has been a rainy and hot summer, and it's not stopping. This upcoming week will feature high temperatures and afternoon showers for South Jerseyans, according to the National Weather Service.
For Saturday, Aug. 8, the NWS has issued a heat advisory until 8 p.m. The temperature will reach 92 degrees, but the day will have a "feels-like" temperature of 101 degrees.
The high humidity is bringing the rain out for South Jersey, with dew points – that muggy feeling you get when you go outside – ranging from the mid-70s to low 90s throughout the week.
Daily chances of thunderstorms means there is "at least a marginalized risk" for heavy rainfall, which could lead to flash flooding and strong wind gusts.
Showers and thunderstorms are also expected Saturday afternoon, so any park or beach plans should end before 5 p.m. The storms will mainly hit before 9 p.m., according to the National Weather Service. The entire day has a 30% chance of precipitation.
Sunday will be a much better day to get outside. It may be foggy in the morning before 8, but otherwise, Sunday will be mostly sunny with a high temperature of 93 degrees.
The night will be clear, with temperatures dropping to around 71 degrees and calm winds.
Monday and Tuesday also will be warm, with temperatures in the low 90s. Monday will be mainly sunny, with a slight chance of showers before 11 p.m. and then a chance of storms later into the night.
Similar precipitation conditions continue on Tuesday night. The day will be sunny, with a chance of rain and storms before 8 p.m., then lighter rain continuing into the night.
Wednesday will be cooler, with an expected high temperature of 88 degrees. Rain is likely after 2 p.m. and could continue until 2 a.m.
Thursday and Friday may be the only dry days of the week and would probably be the most comfortable for an outdoor outing. Rain is not expected, and temperatures both days sit in the mid- to high 80s.
